Public Beta Windows Desktop AES-256-GCM Fully Offline

Your private files, sealed behind one password.

Nexus is an encrypted personal vault for Windows — files, passwords, notes, bookmarks, and contacts, protected by AES-256 encryption and stored entirely on your machine. No cloud. No sync. No internet connection, ever.

View on GitHub → Get Beta Access

Lock Screen — the first thing every Nexus user sees

The Problem

Most "secure" tools still trust someone else with your data.

Password managers, note apps, file vaults — most of them are excellent at security in one narrow sense: encryption in transit. But the data still lives on someone else's server. A breach, a policy change, a shutdown, a subpoena — any of these can expose what was supposed to be private.

I wanted something different: a single vault for the things that actually matter — files, passwords, notes, bookmarks, contacts — that never leaves the device it's created on. Not "encrypted in the cloud." Not stored locally either. Built so there's no cloud to begin with.

AES-256
GCM ENCRYPTION

The Solution

One vault. Everything sealed behind a single master password.

Nexus runs as a single portable file — no installer, no runtime dependencies. Download it, run it, create a vault. Your master password is the only one you need to remember; everything else lives behind it, encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM and decrypted only in memory while the vault is unlocked.

Dashboard
Vault health, storage breakdown, recent files, and live security status at a glance.
Shown with demo data
◆
Credentials Manager
Passwords, usernames, and built-in TOTP for two-factor codes — no separate authenticator app needed.
◇
Secure Notes & Journal
Markdown-formatted encrypted notes, plus a private daily journal with a 30-day calendar view.
◈
Zero-Trace Launcher
Run any app through Nexus in a monitored session — temp files are securely deleted when you're done.
◉
Streamer Mode
Makes Nexus invisible to screen capture, OBS, and screenshots — your vault stays private even on stream.
Security, Made Visible

Trust isn't a claim — it's a status you can check.

Most encrypted apps ask you to trust them blindly. Nexus surfaces its own integrity constantly: a tamper-proof activity log with a cryptographic HMAC chain, a live vault integrity scan, and a real-time security panel — so "secure" isn't just a word in the marketing, it's a number you can watch update.

Security Center

Challenges

Building "offline by design" is harder than it sounds.

01
No server means no easy recovery
Forgotten password with no recovery key configured means the vault genuinely cannot be unlocked — by design. That's the tradeoff of true zero-trust: Nexus ships a Recovery Key system precisely because there's no "reset password" email to fall back on.
02
Proving "we can't see your data" without a server to prove it on
Most privacy claims are backed by a policy document. Nexus backs it with architecture — zero network calls means there's no endpoint to audit because there's nothing to send. The activity log and integrity scan exist so users can verify this for themselves, not just take it on faith.
03
Designing a UI dense enough for power users, calm enough for daily use
A vault holding files, passwords, notes, journal, bookmarks, and contacts risks becoming cluttered fast. The v2 redesign reorganized the sidebar into Vault / System / Personal groups specifically to keep that complexity navigable without flattening it.
Current Status & What's Next

In public beta now. Full release this summer.

Nexus is in active public beta — license keys are free during this phase via Discord, and early Founder-status beta users keep free access permanently once the paid version ships. The v2 UI redesign covered in this case study is complete; remaining work is final auditing and polish before the public release.

Released — Active Development Open Source · MIT Free Forever Windows / Electron

Your canvas. Your references.

Kanvaz is a visual research workspace for collecting, organizing, and connecting references — built the way artists actually work: a fast, distraction-free canvas, not a cluttered asset manager.

View on GitHub → Download Latest

An empty board, ready for references — drag, drop, or paste directly

Why It Exists

Built for the people I work alongside.

Before Kanvaz was a public release, it was a gift — built for the VFX and 3D community I'm part of, for the friends and teachers who needed a fast, no-friction place to drop reference images while working. Most reference tools are either too heavyweight or built for a different workflow entirely.

Kanvaz does one thing: give you a canvas, let you throw images, GIFs, and video references onto it, and stay out of your way.

"Built for VFX artists, 3D artists, and the people who teach them."

What's Inside

Simple on the surface, configurable underneath.

The canvas itself stays minimal by default — dot grid, drop zone, nothing competing for attention. But every detail of how it behaves is adjustable: autosave interval, default card sizing, whether double-clicking creates a note, even whether deleting a card asks for confirmation first.

Settings
Every behavior is a toggle — nothing locked in.
About Kanvaz

Status

Actively developed, not "finished and abandoned."

Kanvaz is at v3.6.9. Board View, the Connection System, and the Connection Inspector are stable and shipping. Map View — a node-editor graph of your whole reference set — is functional and under active polish. No subscription, no feature paywall, no telemetry, no internet connection required. Your files never leave your machine, and it stays free forever either way.

04

What's next

🏷️

Editable tags & custom properties

Tags and custom properties already exist in the data model — the editing UI is the planned headline feature for v4.0.

🔌

Map View connection-wire fix

Wires occasionally start from a slightly different point than the actual output port. Reported by users, reproduction and root-cause investigation in progress.

🎬

Broader video codec support

MKV and AVI don't currently play due to a Chromium codec limitation — MP4 (H.264) and WebM are recommended in the meantime.

🖊️

Annotation toolbar tracking

The annotation toolbar doesn't currently follow the canvas if you pan or zoom while it's open — a known, tracked fix.

About

Developer by discipline.
3D artist by training.
Builder by default.

I'm Atharva Patil. I write software that encrypts and protects, build tools that help artists work faster, and study how to render light convincingly — all at the same time, all from Navi Mumbai.

Most people choose a lane. I haven't figured out why I should. The same instinct that goes into designing Nexus's lock screen goes into lighting a 3D scene — obsessing over how things feel when you interact with them, not just how they look. Kanvaz started as a tool I built for the VFX community I'm part of. Obscura started because Roblox developers deserve professional-grade tooling without a paywall. Every project comes from being inside the problem.

I run Northbyte Studios — a solo software operation. Everything ships free forever or open source. Not as a strategy. As a principle.

Veris Released

Offline-first, explainable security investigation platform for Windows. Built around deterministic analysis and evidence-based conclusions instead of black-box AI scoring — every finding traces back to concrete evidence.

TypeScriptNode.jsSQLiteModular Monorepo

Tech Stack

  • TypeScript on Node.js
  • Modular monorepo — independently testable packages

  • Vitest, ESLint, Prettier for testing and code quality

Engineering Highlights

  • Deterministic analysis engine — no black-box AI scoring or cloud lookups

  • AI intentionally limited to a read-only explanation layer — it never performs detection or influences results
  • Offline-first with no mandatory cloud dependency and no telemetry
  • Package boundaries with deterministic APIs and comprehensive testing across core domain models, analysis engine, correlation engine, risk engine, and explainability engine

Role / Ownership

Solo developer. System architecture, security design, software engineering, package design, API design, testing strategy, documentation, UX planning, and performance planning.

TypeScriptNode.jsOpen SourceMIT

Role / Ownership

Accessibility

What's actually done, and what honestly isn't yet.

A checklist that only lists the good parts isn't a statement, it's marketing. This page is kept current with the real state of the site — including the gaps.

Target

WCAG 2.1 Level AA. Not independently audited by a third party — this is a self-assessment, kept honest by listing specific gaps below rather than a blanket "compliant" claim.

Implemented

  • Every custom interactive element — the 7 expandable resume/project cards, the contact-page dropdowns, all buttons, nav, and links — is keyboard-reachable with a visible :focus-visible state, not just a mouse target with an onclick.
  • Resume/project cards use role="button", tabindex="0", and correct aria-expanded state, activated by Enter and Space as well as click.
  • The custom dropdowns on the Contact page follow the real ARIA listbox pattern (role="listbox", role="option", aria-selected, roving highlight via arrow keys) rather than a native <select> or an unlabelled div stack.
  • A skip-to-content link is reachable by keyboard and actually becomes visible on focus — it isn't hidden off-screen permanently.
  • All animation on the site (background effects, ring/logo motion, hero typewriter, card tilt) respects prefers-reduced-motion and disables itself accordingly.

Try it yourself

Rather than just claim keyboard accessibility works, here's a way to feel it directly — a live caption showing approximately what a screen reader would announce as you Tab through this page. Not a substitute for testing with real assistive tech, but closer than a sentence.

Known gaps — not yet fixed

  • Color contrast has not had a full pass yet — some muted text/border combinations are on the roadmap to verify against AA ratios, not yet confirmed.
  • This is a single-page app with in-memory routing (a deliberate tradeoff for portability, not an oversight) — because every page's markup coexists in one DOM, there are multiple <h1> elements on one document at once, which can make the heading outline confusing for screen-reader users navigating by heading.
  • Navigating between pages updates the document title but doesn't yet move focus or announce the change via a live region — keyboard/screen-reader users won't get an explicit "you're on a new page" signal beyond the title change.

Report an issue

If something here doesn't work with your keyboard, screen reader, or assistive tech — email me directly. Real reports move up the list faster than anything on this page.

v3.21 Kanvaz content updated with real v3.6.9 release data

The Kanvaz case-study page previously claimed "development is complete, final release" and listed fabricated future features. Updated every mention site-wide using the actual v3.6.9 GitHub release notes and README — status, tech details, and a real roadmap (editable tags in v4, Map View wire-alignment fix) pulled from documented "known limitations," not guessed at.

v3.18 CLS regression fixed, mobile ring alignment bug fixed

Root-caused a real measured CLS of 1.032 to font-display:swap on the Google Fonts request — switched to font-display:optional, eliminating the late-reflow shift entirely. Also fixed a genuine mobile bug: the About-page ring elements weren't resizing with their container and were overflowing on small screens.

v3.16 Console error resolved, og:image prepped

Closed a console error open since v3.6 — root cause was a view-source link attempting window.open('view-source:...'), which Chrome blocks at the browser level (not a catchable JS exception, so the fallback never ran). Also composed a proper 1200×630 social-card image, ready for when hosting goes live.

v3.1 Full accessibility pass

Made 7 previously mouse-only expandable cards fully keyboard-accessible, added :focus-visible site-wide, fixed a skip-to-content link that was permanently hidden off-screen, and unified two inconsistent badge components into one.
